- Fixed `read_file` tool returning an unhelpful error when given a directory path; it now suggests using `list_directory` instead. ([#54303](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/54303); thanks [Prohect](https://github.com/Prohect))
- Fixed a bug where a thread within the currently active project would flash upon cmd-clicking the project header. ([#55190](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55190))
- Fixed a bug where placeholder text in the agent panel's message editor wouldn't properly wrap. ([#55125](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55125))
- Fixed a bug where the context menu in the agent panel (and other scrollable surfaces) would appear at the wrong location. ([#55124](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55124))
- Fixed a bug where subfolders of a repository were not displayed in the title bar's project button. ([#54796](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/54796))
- Fixed a rare panic when invoking Helix motions on an editor that had not yet been laid out. ([#55816](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55816))
- Fixed absolute path mentions in `acp_thread` so direct file references (including `:line` and `#Lline` formats) now open correctly instead of resolving to invalid/empty files. ([#53229](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/53229); thanks [Revantark](https://github.com/Revantark))
- Fixed GitHub avatar lookup for bot noreply commit authors. ([#55297](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55297); thanks [tsutoringo](https://github.com/tsutoringo))
- Fixed plan and edited-files lists in the agent panel being squashed when they contain many items. ([#55189](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55189); thanks [HalavicH](https://github.com/HalavicH))
- Fixed shell environment loading when login shells exit non-zero after printing environment variables. ([#55175](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55175))

- Fixed the recent projects list jumping to the top after deleting a project, so you can now bulk-delete entries by repeatedly clicking the delete icon or pressing the keybind. ([#54777](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/54777))

- Fixed ACP agents failing to launch on Windows with "The system cannot find the file specified." ([#55946](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55946))
- Fixed inotify event queue overflows on Linux. ([#55941](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55941))
- Fixed local zeta2 edit predictions using the wrong prompt format. ([#56191](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/56191))

ClawX - Graphical AI Assistant based on OpenClaw

issue_insights.summary_brief: 跨仓库层面，OpenRouter Sonnet 评估回归问题已影响 159 个仓库（生成轨迹为空、结果 0/32），同时 OpenRouter 配置下仍消耗 OpenHands 积分的问题波及 28 个仓库，存在未预期的成本泄露风险。此外，get_function_call 对字符串参数的空格裁剪问题破坏了文件编辑工具功能，影响 6 个仓库的 tool_call_protocol 规范。安全方面，agno ClickHouse 矢量数据库存在 SQL 注入漏洞，可导致全表数据删除；opencode 存在 external_directory 权限绕过漏洞。单仓层面，P0 级别问题集中于工作流运行时崩溃、会话状态静默丢失及启动失败三大类。
global_highlights: 安全高风险：agno ClickHouse SQL 注入可构造恒真 WHERE 条件删除全表数据；opencode external_directory 在跨盘符路径下权限检查失效；anomalyco/opencode 模型余额充足但 API 返回 402 暗示上游计费异常
工作流运行时断裂：anthropic-sdk-python 的 append_messages 内部调用导致 Tool Runner 无限循环；agno Session Storage 异常处理吞掉 DB 错误后静默丢弃用户聊天历史；claude-code-action 约 70% 失败率因 gh CLI 缺 --repo 参数

启动阻断集中爆发：anomalyco/opencode TUI "No renderer found" Fatal Error 完全阻断主界面；claude-code-action restore-config 因缺少父目录触发 cpSync ENOENT 崩溃；agno-agi/agno CI 全部 11 个 test_code_chunking 测试因 tree_sitter_language_pack API 变更失败
SDK 与工具链兼容性问题：claude-agent-sdk-typescript 在 glibc 系统上错误优先选择 musl 二进制导致 ENOENT；anthropic-claude-code MCP 工具调用将数组/对象参数序列化为 JSON 字符串违反 MCP 规范；多个 SDK 的 Zod v4 兼容性导致文档字段描述丢失

source_issues.title: [Vulnerability] SQL Injection in agno ClickHouse Vector Database via `delete_by_metadata`

A payload like {'source': "' OR '1'='1"} generates a tautology WHERE clause, deleting ALL rows in the table. The PoC confirms mass deletion of all vector embeddings. While table/database names use safe parameterization, the WHERE clause is completely unescaped.

source_issues.title: `external_directory` permission bypassed for cross-drive paths on Windows

Contains() incorrectly returns true for cross-drive paths because path.relative() returns the full absolute path. Demonstrates write to C:\Users\...\Desktop\test.md succeeds while write to D:\test.md (same drive, outside workspace) is correctly rejected. Security boundary violated on v1.14.49 and v1.14.50.

top_pain_points.topic: get_function_call strips whitespace from string arguments, breaking file editing tools
top_pain_points.summary: get_function_call applies .strip() to every string argument before passing to tool function. Tools that perform file replacement with newline-containing strings receive empty strings and raise misleading 'old_string must not be empty' errors.
aliases: MCP tool call array/object arguments wrongly stringified
concurrent hook execution breaks chaining pattern
top_pain_points.review_reason: This bug blocks file editing workflows — a key feature. When an LLM tries to replace text containing newlines, the .strip() call converts '\n\n' to '', causing a 'old_string must not be empty' error. The LLM retries infinitely with the same failure. This is a main flow blockage for any agent using file modification tools, with misleading error messages that suggest the LLM made a bad call when the tool actually corrupted the input.

source_issues.title: Hook dispatch: docs imply sequential, implementations are concurrent
source_issues.evidence: Empirical testing with 3 hooks (600ms, 400ms, 200ms delays) in Python SDK 0.1.72, TypeScript SDK 0.2.126, and third-party Kotlin SDK all show identical concurrent behavior: all hooks enter at same millisecond, exit in reverse order of registration, total wall time equals max delay (600ms) not sum. Source confirms both Python and TypeScript SDKs dispatch control requests via fire-and-forget tasks. Rate-limiter example pattern in official docs is broken by this behavior.

signals.topic: GenerativeModelStore incremental fetch cursor regression causing silent DB egress cost increase
signals.summary: The `_last_fetch_id` cursor in GenerativeModelStore daemon regresses whenever a low-ID model is updated, causing subsequent polls to re-fetch all rows between the regressed cursor and the true high-water mark. This silently defeats the daemon's documented purpose of reducing DB egress in cloud environments, resulting in unexpected cost overhead.
aliases: DB egress savings defeated by cursor bug
signals.review_reason: This is a functional bug with documented cost impact. The incremental fetch cursor silently regresses on every poll where a low-ID model is the only update, causing the next poll to re-fetch all intervening rows. This defeats the daemon's explicit purpose (reducing DB egress in cloud deployments) and produces measurable cost overhead. The bug is reproducible, has clear steps, and the impact is concrete: wasted DB egress on every regression cycle.

source_issues.title: GenerativeModelStore: _last_fetch_id can regress and defeat incremental fetch
source_issues.evidence: When a low-ID existing model is the only thing updated in a poll, _last_fetch_id regresses to that lower ID, causing the next poll to re-fetch all rows 6..N. This silently breaks the 'reduce DB egress' purpose of the daemon, creating direct cost overhead in cloud environments every time the regression occurs.

signals.topic: Session storage exception handling silently drops session data on transient DB failures

signals.topic: get_function_call strips whitespace from string arguments, breaking file editing tools
signals.summary: get_function_call applies .strip() to every string argument before passing to tool function. Tools that perform file replacement with newline-containing strings receive empty strings and raise misleading 'old_string must not be empty' errors.
signals.review_reason: This bug blocks file editing workflows — a key feature. When an LLM tries to replace text containing newlines, the .strip() call converts '\n\n' to '', causing a 'old_string must not be empty' error. The LLM retries infinitely with the same failure. This is a main flow blockage for any agent using file modification tools, with misleading error messages that suggest the LLM made a bad call when the tool actually corrupted the input.

signals.topic: SQL injection in ClickHouse vector database delete_by_metadata allows mass data deletion
signals.summary: delete_by_metadata directly interpolates metadata keys and values into raw SQL via f-strings. A payload like {'source': "' OR '1'='1"} generates a tautology WHERE clause, deleting ALL rows in the table.
aliases: mass vector data deletion via SQLi
signals.review_reason: Confirmed SQL injection vulnerability with working PoC that demonstrates mass deletion of all vector embeddings. The attacker can inject a tautology condition via metadata value to delete ALL rows — not theoretical, the PoC shows it in action. Priority P1 (not P0) because count=1, single repo, and exploitation requires attacker control of metadata values rather than being universally triggered. However, the confirmed mass data loss and active PoC clearly meet the user impact threshold.

signals.topic: external_directory permission bypass for cross-drive paths on Windows — security vulnerability
signals.summary: On Windows, when the workspace is on one drive (e.g., D:), tools bypass the external_directory permission check for paths on other drives (e.g., C:). The root cause is that Node.js path.relative() returns the full absolute path for cross-drive scenarios, causing contains() to incorrectly return true. Files on C: that users intended to restrict are accessible without permission prompts, creating a security boundary violation.
signals.review_reason: A detailed bug report with confirmed root cause in packages/core/src/filesystem.ts shows that external_directory permission checks are bypassed for all cross-drive paths on Windows. The security boundary that users rely on to prevent unauthorized file access is completely ineffective — writing to sensitive locations like C:\Users\Desktop is allowed without any permission prompt. While count=1 and single-repo, the security impact (unauthorized file access) with full root-cause analysis and reproduction steps qualifies this as P1.

source_issues.title: `external_directory` permission bypassed for cross-drive paths on Windows
source_issues.evidence: On Windows with workspace on D: drive, the external_directory permission gate is bypassed for all paths on C: drive. Contains() incorrectly returns true for cross-drive paths because path.relative() returns the full absolute path. Demonstrates write to C:\Users\...\Desktop\test.md succeeds while write to D:\test.md (same drive, outside workspace) is correctly rejected. Security boundary violated on v1.14.49 and v1.14.50.

While count=1 and single-repo, the regression evidence (worked before, broken now) and complete startup block on a specific Linux distribution warrants P1.

source_issues.evidence: Regression: worked in 1.14.48, broken in 1.14.50. Error: 'Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: getcontext: symbol not found'. Alpine Linux uses musl libc which lacks the getcontext symbol. TUI completely fails to start. Confirmed on Alpine edge x86_64.

signals.topic: Files list API 无法列出 Managed Agent 中的文件，缺少必要的 beta header 支持
signals.summary: 用户在使用 Managed Agent API 时无法通过 Files list API 列出文件，原因是 FileServiceImpl 始终使用默认 beta header，缺少 `managed-agents-2026-04-01`，且无任何方式覆盖该 header，导致该功能完全不可用。
aliases: Files list API missing managed-agents beta header
Cannot list files from managed agent scope
signals.review_reason: 这是一个明确的用户功能阻断问题：用户使用 Managed Agent API 时无法列出文件，且 SDK 层无任何 workaround，导致该具体场景功能完全不可用。虽 count=1（单仓单 issue），但影响明确属于功能缺失导致的可用性问题，符合 P1 判定标准。

source_issues.title: Files list API does not support listing files from managed agent API
source_issues.evidence: 用户在使用 Managed Agent API 时无法列出文件，FileServiceImpl 始终添加默认 beta header，缺少 managed-agents-2026-04-01，且无任何 override 机制，导致该场景功能完全不可用。

signals.topic: Tool Runner loop infinite loop when append_messages() is called inside the loop
signals.summary: Calling runner.append_messages() inside the tool runner loop sets _messages_modified=True, causing __run__ to skip auto-append of assistant message + tool result. The next iteration sends a request with no tool result in history, so Claude re-triggers the tool call, creating an infinite loop. The official 'Advanced usage' documentation example is inconsistent with the correct pattern shown in the 'Modifying tool results' example.
aliases: tool runner advanced usage doc bug
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：tool runner loop 无限循环，用户主流程完全无法推进。文档示例错误，具有广泛误导性。

source_issues.title: [Bug] append_messages() inside tool runner loop causes infinite loop (advanced usage docs example)
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed with minimal repro. Calling append_messages() inside loop sets _messages_modified=True, skipping auto-append of tool result. Infinite loop confirmed — tool result never reaches history. Official docs example is inconsistent with correct pattern.

signals.topic: ServerToolResult not delivered when client tools interrupt the streaming turn
signals.summary: When server-side tools (code_execution, web_search) and client-defined tools run concurrently in the same turn, the ServerToolResult blocks are never delivered to the caller — neither during streaming nor in the final message. This leaves orphaned server_tool_use blocks with no matching result, causing front-end stuck spinners and false error detections in production load tests.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：streaming 模式下 server tool 结果丢失，生产环境反复出现（5并发用户测试均复现）。前端 stuck spinners 和误报错误是明确的用户可感知影响。

source_issues.title: ServerToolResult not delivered when client tools interrupt the stream (code_execution + client tool concurrency)
source_issues.evidence: Production load test evidence: 5 concurrent users, orphaned server_tool_use blocks in every test case. Front-end stuck spinners and incorrect error detection confirmed. Workaround requires heuristic cleanup — API contract is violated.

signals.topic: Thinking + structured output + tool use combination produces invalid responses and blocks structured parsing
signals.summary: When using thinking (extended/adaptive), structured output (json_schema), and tool use together in multi-turn conversations, two bugs occur: (1) model emits thinking block + empty text block with stop_reason='end_turn' instead of tool_use blocks, causing SDK's messages.parse to fail; (2) final text block contains invalid JSON (mixed content, partial JSON with blank lines). The interaction between these three features is broken and unreliable in production.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：thinking+structured output+tools 三者组合时，结构化 JSON 输出完全不可靠（频繁产生无效 JSON），messages.parse 失败。生产环境无法使用该组合。

source_issues.title: Structured output + thinking + tool use: two bugs in multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: 模型在 thinking+structured output+tools 组合下频繁出现：tool_use blocks 不发出（仅 thinking+空文本块），或最终 JSON 输出无效（含重复/部分内容）。messages.parse 抛出异常，无法获得结构化输出。用户明确表示'在生产环境难以可靠使用'。

signals.topic: Managed Agents sessions.events.send does not accept output_config/effort parameter — no parity with messages.create
signals.summary: The Managed Agents endpoint (client.beta.sessions.events.send) rejects the output_config parameter with HTTP 400, while client.messages.create accepts it. Users cannot control 'effort' (thinking depth) on managed agents, forcing reliance on opaque platform defaults. Empirical data shows 3x cost increase ($0.31 vs $0.10) and 3.3x latency (156s vs 47s) compared to steered runs. No workaround exists — even extra_body is blocked by server-side validation.
signals.review_reason: 明显成本损失（3倍）和延迟损失（3.3倍）。API 不一致：messages.create 支持但 managed agents 不支持，无任何变通方案。

source_issues.title: Managed Agents sessions.events.send rejects output_config with 400 — no parity with messages.create for effort/thinking control
source_issues.evidence: 成本差异3倍（$0.31 vs $0.10），延迟差异3.3倍（156s vs 47s），经生产烟雾测试验证。extra_body逃逸阀也被服务端严格校验拦截。用户无法控制thinking深度，平台默认不可读、不可配置。

signals.topic: PDF processing ignores citations.enabled=false and uses Visual Mode instead of Text Extraction
signals.summary: When users set citations.enabled=false in PDF document objects to request text-only extraction (Text Extraction mode, no visual processing), Claude still processes the PDF using Visual Mode. This results in significantly higher token usage and potentially different content interpretation. Disabling citations does not prevent visual mode as documented.
aliases: PDF text extraction mode not respected
signals.review_reason: 体验下降+成本损失：PDF处理模式与文档承诺不符，导致token消耗异常增加。用户意图（文本提取）与实际行为（视觉模式）不一致。

source_issues.title: Claude reads PDF using Visual Mode even if citations are disabled
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确设置 citations.enabled=false，意图使用文本提取模式（非视觉模式），但模型仍使用视觉模式处理PDF。token使用量异常高（高于纯文本处理预期），且对扫描PDF产生图像理解而非文本识别结果。

signals.topic: toolRunner drops defaultHeaders on follow-up requests, breaking proxy/gateway authentication
signals.summary: client.messages.toolRunner does not forward defaultHeaders on subsequent API calls during the tool-use loop, causing authentication failures when using proxies or gateways that rely on custom headers (e.g., Cloudflare AI Gateway's cf-aig-authorization).
aliases: toolRunner defaultHeaders dropped on follow-up calls
toolRunner missing headers in tool-use loop
signals.review_reason: This is a clear user pain point: toolRunner silently drops custom auth headers on every follow-up API call in the tool-use loop, causing authentication failures in production proxy/gateway setups. The failure is non-obvious because the first call succeeds. Cloudflare team explicitly confirmed this as an SDK-side bug, and the workaround (manual loop) requires significant code changes. This blocks the core multi-turn tool-use workflow behind proxies.

source_issues.title: `toolRunner` drops `defaultHeaders` on follow-up requests (breaks proxy/gateway setups)
source_issues.evidence: First API call includes defaultHeaders correctly, but subsequent calls in the tool-use loop drop them, causing authentication_error. Confirmed by Cloudflare team as SDK-side bug. Affects Cloudflare AI Gateway unified billing and BYOK setups. Users must implement tool-use loop manually as workaround.

signals.topic: Vertex AI: document URL sources rejected with misleading error path
signals.summary: Using @anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk with document content blocks with URL sources causes the Vertex AI endpoint to reject the request, with an incorrect error path pointing to image.source.base64.data instead of the actual document.url field, making debugging significantly harder.
aliases: Vertex SDK document URL source rejected
wrong error path for document URL source on Vertex
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point: document URL sources are explicitly documented as supported but the Vertex AI endpoint rejects them at runtime, AND the error message points to the wrong field (image.source.base64.data instead of the actual document.url field), making it extremely hard to diagnose. This blocks users from using a documented feature on the Vertex SDK variant.

source_issues.title: Vertex AI: document URL sources rejected with incorrect error path
source_issues.evidence: Payload with document content block using URL source is rejected by Vertex AI endpoint with error referencing image.source.base64.data (wrong field path). User had to debug blindly due to the misleading error. The documentation lists URL sources as supported but the endpoint rejects them.

signals.topic: zodOutputFormat fails when project uses zod3
signals.summary: zodOutputFormat throws an error when called with a zod3 (v3.x) schema, breaking output format validation in projects that depend on zod v3.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point for projects using zod v3: zodOutputFormat is a key helper for structured output, and it fails silently (throws) when used with the widely-adopted zod v3. Note: the issue is now closed (resolved), so this is a borderline P2. Keeping it as it represents real breakage for zod v3 users until the fix is released. Downgraded to P2 due to single occurrence and resolved status.

source_issues.title: zodOutputFormat fails when project uses zod3
source_issues.evidence: Calling zodOutputFormat with a zod3 (zod v3.x) schema throws an error, while zod v4 schemas work. Reproduced with a Stackblitz demo. Issue is closed (resolved).

signals.topic: Query crashes with MessageParseError when thinking block lacks signature field on non-Anthropic-compatible backends
signals.summary: SDK parser assumes every thinking content block has a 'signature' field and crashes with KeyError/MessageParseError when a third-party backend (e.g. GPT-5.4 via Anthropic-compatible API) emits a thinking block without one. The query fails mid-execution with no graceful fallback, blocking the main flow entirely for affected backends.
aliases: KeyError signature in thinking block parser
signals.review_reason: Main flow is completely blocked for users of non-Anthropic-compatible backends. The query crashes with a KeyError/MessageParseError at the parser level with no recovery path. The user explicitly reports the request runs ~30 seconds then fails before any result is returned. This is a confirmed, reproducible crash in the core query() API path affecting a documented use case (Anthropic-compatible API backends). Single-issue P0 justified by severity (complete flow block), clear user impact (query fails entirely), and existence of a reproducible sample.

source_issues.title: MessageParseError: missing signature in thinking block with claude-agent-sdk 0.1.79 and Anthropic-compatible backend
source_issues.evidence: Query crashes with KeyError: 'signature' in message_parser.py line 104 during normal usage (repository URL processing). Users of GPT-5.4 via Anthropic-compatible backend are blocked from completing any query. Reproduced on latest SDK version 0.1.79.

signals.topic: TaskNotificationMessage fires prematurely while subagent is still executing, causing orchestrator to dispatch wrong downstream actions and waste compute
signals.summary: When an orchestrator dispatches multiple subagents in parallel via the Task tool, TaskNotificationMessage/<task-notification> is sometimes delivered to the orchestrator before the subagent has finished all tool calls. The orchestrator treats the premature notification as a completion signal, immediately dispatching downstream agents against files that don't exist yet, causing cascading failures and wasted compute. In one incident, this resulted in ~8 minutes of wasted re-execution and $21.51 cost for a single run.
signals.review_reason: Severe functional breakdown in the core Task/orchestrator workflow. The orchestrator receives a false completion signal and dispatches incorrect downstream agents against files that haven't been written yet, directly causing wasted compute (re-execution of 5 subagents) and financial loss ($21.51 incident cost). This is the SDK's primary multi-agent orchestration feature producing actively wrong behavior. Single-issue P0 justified by: the issue is in the SDK's core Task orchestration, produces wrong results (not just degraded), causes measurable financial loss, and is reproducible in a realistic production scenario.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Orchestrator received premature <task-notification> while subagent was mid-execution (tool 13 of 39, 466 seconds remaining). This caused: (1) downstream reviewers dispatched against non-existent files, (2) all 5 researchers re-dispatched (~8 min wasted), (3) orchestrator flooded with stale notifications. Single incident cost $21.51 vs $22.33 baseline with correct behavior. Non-deterministic but confirmed reproducible in production-like environment.

signals.topic: TRACEPARENT context silently dropped on 2nd+ query() call in long-running processes, fragmenting distributed telemetry
signals.summary: In a long-running Python server/worker process, the bundled Claude Code CLI correctly honors TRACEPARENT and nests spans under the caller's trace on the first query() call. On all subsequent calls, the same valid TRACEPARENT is silently ignored and CLI spans become orphaned roots with fresh trace IDs. This breaks the Read agent traces observability flow described in the SDK documentation for the dominant production deployment shape.
aliases: TRACEPARENT silently ignored on repeated query calls
distributed trace context dropped after first call
OpenTelemetry span orphaning in long-running SDK processes
signals.review_reason: Telemetry fragmentation breaks observability in the exact production deployment shape documented in the SDK's own hosting docs (long-running server/worker). The issue is 100% reproducible, silently degrades tracing (no error thrown), and makes the Read agent traces flow entirely unusable past the first query call. While not a crash, this is a significant reliability/observability gap for production users, and the 'silently' nature (no error, just wrong data) makes it insidious. P1 rather than P0 because it does not block the main query flow — results are correct, only telemetry is broken.

source_issues.title: Bundled CLI silently drops inbound TRACEPARENT on 2nd+ query() call when ~/.claude/ has state from a prior run
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible: first query() call nests CLI spans correctly under TRACEPARENT trace; all subsequent calls produce orphaned CLI spans with fresh trace IDs and no parent. Triggered by persistent state in ~/.claude/. Reproduced with both auto-injected and explicit TRACEPARENT. Directly breaks the observability flow documented in 'Read agent traces' and 'Hosting the Agent SDK' docs for long-running server processes.

signals.topic: Hook dispatch executes concurrently despite documentation stating sequential execution, breaking rate-limiting and audit-logging patterns
signals.summary: The official SDK documentation explicitly states 'Hooks execute in the order they appear in the array' and uses a chained pattern (rate-limiter → auth → sanitizer → audit) as a core example. Empirically, all registered hook matchers on the same event fire simultaneously with no temporal ordering. This breaks any sequential-dependency pattern including rate limiting, authorization checks, and ordered audit logging.
aliases: concurrent hook execution breaks chaining pattern
signals.review_reason: The documented hook chaining pattern is fundamentally broken — rate-limiters cannot gate requests, auth checks cannot run before input sanitization, audit logs cannot fire last. This is not a documentation-only issue: the documented example pattern will not work as intended. The issue affects all three SDK implementations (Python, TypeScript, Kotlin) confirming it is a protocol-level design issue, not an isolated bug. P1 due to functional breakage of a core SDK feature (hooks) despite being single-issue.

source_issues.title: Hook dispatch: docs imply sequential, implementations are concurrent
source_issues.evidence: Empirical testing with 3 hooks (600ms, 400ms, 200ms delays) in Python SDK 0.1.72, TypeScript SDK 0.2.126, and third-party Kotlin SDK all show identical concurrent behavior: all hooks enter at same millisecond, exit in reverse order of registration, total wall time equals max delay (600ms) not sum. Source confirms both Python and TypeScript SDKs dispatch control requests via fire-and-forget tasks. Rate-limiter example pattern in official docs is broken by this behavior.

signals.topic: StructuredOutput tool intermittently wraps response in redundant 'output' field causing schema validation to fail
signals.summary: When using structured outputs with output_format, the StructuredOutput tool non-deterministically wraps user data in an extra {"output": {...}} field. When the wrapper is present, ResultMessage.structured_output is None and the agent sees conflicting validation errors (required field 'actions' exists but is inside an invalid 'output' wrapper). This causes agent confusion, flaky results, and prompts that succeed or fail randomly with identical inputs.
aliases: output field wrapping in structured responses
signals.review_reason: Intermittent but recurring schema validation failures corrupt structured output data, leave ResultMessage.structured_output as None, and cause the agent to degrade its own output (47 items → 1 item). The non-deterministic nature makes it extremely hard for users to diagnose and reproduce. P1 rather than P0 because the failure is intermittent (not every call crashes) and the main query() call completes — only the structured output feature is unreliable.

source_issues.title: [BUG] StructuredOutput tool wraps data in 'output' field causing schema validation to fail
source_issues.evidence: Non-deterministic: identical prompts produce either valid {"actions": [...]} or invalid {"output": {"actions": [...]}}. When wrapper present, structured_output is None and agent receives confusing validation errors. Agent 'debugged' by reducing output from 47 items to 1 item in attempt to fix. 11 comments indicate ongoing discussion and impact.

signals.topic: Linux glibc 系统上 native binary picker 错误选择 musl 变体导致 spawn ENOENT 失败
signals.summary: 在 glibc Linux（如 Ubuntu 24.04）上，SDK 的 binary picker 在 pnpm 安装了 musl 和 glibc 两个可选包时，优先尝试 musl 变体。由于 musl 二进制在 glibc 系统上无法执行（缺少 /lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1），spawn 时抛出 ENOENT，导致主流程 query() 完全失败，且错误信息误导用户认为二进制缺失而非 libc 不匹配。30-50% 的缓存未命中安装中发生此问题。
aliases: musl binary preferred over glibc on glibc Linux
libc detection missing in binary resolver
binary picker selects wrong libc variant on Linux
signals.review_reason: count=3 达高频阈值，主流程 query() 在 Linux glibc 系统上因 libc 不匹配直接阻断，spawn ENOENT 导致会话无法运行，符合 P0 条件：有样例链接支撑、多版本受影响（v0.2.116、v0.2.126、v0.2.138）、错误信息误导用户认为二进制缺失而非 libc 问题

source_issues.title: Binary picker selects musl variant on glibc Linux, causing ENOENT at spawn

signals.topic: createSdkMcpServer 在 Zod v4 下丢失嵌套字段及动态注册工具的 .describe() 元数据
signals.summary: createSdkMcpServer 的 Zod -> JSON Schema 转换路径不兼容 Zod v4 的元数据存储方式（instance metadata 而非 _def.description）。问题影响两层：(1) 嵌套属性字段的描述丢失，顶层 shape 值描述能正确回填但嵌套结构中丢失；(2) 通过 registerTool 动态注册的工具描述也丢失，因为回填仅在 createSdkMcpServer 调用时执行一次。这导致 MCP tools/list 响应中模型看不到字段级指引，工具可用性下降。

Zod v4 metadata not preserved in MCP tool schemas

signals.topic: options.hooks 导致 agent 忽略自定义 systemPrompt，身份识别漂移为 'Claude Code'

agent ignores custom persona when any hook is used

signals.topic: restore-config.ts cpSync crash with ENOENT on CLAUDE.md (missing .claude-pr/ parent dir)
signals.summary: restoreConfigFromBase crashes with ENOENT when the PR head has CLAUDE.md but no .claude/ directory. Since v1.0.89, the loop copies each SENSITIVE_PATH in alphabetical order; copying .claude/ first creates .claude-pr/ as a side-effect of recursive:true, but when .claude/ is absent, cpSync for CLAUDE.md hits a non-existent parent dir and crashes the action.
signals.review_reason: Action crashes (exit code 1) and blocks PR review workflow entirely. Regression introduced in v1.0.89. Reproducible deterministically. No partial workaround within affected versions.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase crashes with ENOENT when only CLAUDE.md exists (cpSync needs mkdir of .claude-pr/ first)
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with exit code 1. Repro: PR whose head contains CLAUDE.md but no .claude/, .mcp.json, etc. Fails deterministically. Regression from v1.0.89 to v1.0.121. Workaround: pin to v1.0.88.

signals.topic: restore-config.ts cpSync crashes when SENSITIVE_PATHS are symlinks (dereference:false)
signals.summary: restoreConfigFromBase crashes with ENOENT when any SENSITIVE_PATH entry is a symlink. cpSync defaults to dereference:false, so it tries to recreate the symlink at .claude-pr/ rather than copying file contents, and fails because the parent directory doesn't exist yet.
signals.review_reason: Action crashes (exit code 1) deterministically when a symlinked SENSITIVE_PATH is present, blocking the entire PR review workflow. Regression from v1.0.89. Same root file (restore-config.ts) as issue #1311, but different trigger condition.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with exit code 1 on repos where CLAUDE.md or other SENSITIVE_PATHS are symlinks (e.g. CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md). Regression from v1.0.89. Workaround: pin to v1.0.88.

signals.topic: claude-code-review workflow ~70% failure rate: gh CLI missing --repo flag and haiku dedup false-positive
signals.summary: Two deterministic failure modes in claude-code-review.yml produce ~70% review failure rate on passing PRs. Mode A: gh pr view/list/issue invoked without --repo causes 'no default remote repository' error when working dir isn't repo root. Mode B: haiku dedup misclassifies absence-of-findings as duplicate and skips posting reviews on trivial PRs.
aliases: claude-code-review workflow failure gh pr view no repo flag
haiku dedup false positive skips no-issue reviews
signals.review_reason: Key workflow feature (claude-code-review) fails on 70% of passing PRs. Both Mode A and Mode B are deterministic, not flaky. Authors receive no review at all on affected PRs. Significant real-world impact on PR review automation.

source_issues.title: claude-code-review.yml has two recurring failure modes (Mode A: gh CLI invocation; Mode B: haiku dedup false-positive)
source_issues.evidence: ~70% review failure rate observed across PRs #62-#74. Both failure modes are deterministic and reproducible. PR author gets no review at all for affected PRs. Concrete failing runs referenced.

signals.topic: Action silently posts raw CLAUDE.md file as review comment instead of structured review output, exits success
signals.summary: Action intermittently echoes the repository's CLAUDE.md file verbatim as the PR comment body instead of the structured review requested by the prompt. Action exits conclusion:success despite no real review being performed. Naive setups (those trusting green check = review happened) silently accept a non-review.
aliases: CLAUDE.md echoed as review comment verbatim
structured review output replaced by memory file dump
signals.review_reason: Key feature (structured code review) silently fails while reporting success. Produces a misleading green checkmark on PRs that have no real review. Distinct from a crash: exits success but delivers zero value. Consumers who trust exit code receive incorrect confidence signals.

source_issues.title: Action posts repo's CLAUDE.md verbatim as comment body instead of structured review (workflow exits success)
source_issues.evidence: Intermittent but reproducible: same prompt on two consecutive commits, first run = structured review, second run = 19,407-char raw CLAUDE.md verbatim. Two concrete run IDs provided (25720844923 vs 25722050413). Exit code: success. Naive workflows that treat green check = review happened silently accept a non-review. Wastes workflow minutes and OAuth quota.

signals.topic: Agent halts with end_turn after Edit/Write phase without invoking Bash, silently completing multi-step prompts with no output
signals.summary: claude-sonnet-4-6 agent reads files, makes Edit/Write calls, creates TodoWrite items, then voluntarily halts with stop_reason:end_turn and empty result — never invoking Bash. Action returns outcome:success. All 7 repro runs produced zero Bash calls vs 42 in the working baseline. No work product is produced but the workflow sees success.
aliases: agent stops after Edit/Write end_turn no Bash
multi-step prompt silent failure outcome success no work product
signals.review_reason: Multi-step prompts silently fail to produce any output (no Bash, no commits, no PRs) while action reports success. This is a silent failure mode that wastes CI minutes and OAuth quota with no indication of what went wrong. Multiple consecutive runs with byte-identical prompts confirm reproducibility.

source_issues.title: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with stop_reason: end_turn, never invokes Bash; multi-step prompts fail to complete (claude-sonnet-4-6)
source_issues.evidence: 7 consecutive reproducible failures with claude-sonnet-4-6 across ~14 hours. Working baseline had 42 Bash invocations; all 7 failed runs had 0 Bash invocations. Empty result string with is_error:false and outcome:success masks the failure entirely. Pending TodoWrite items left incomplete. No PR produced despite explicit multi-step instructions.

signals.topic: VS Code webview crashes with 'Unhandled case: [object Object]' when markdownlint diagnostics contain object-typed Diagnostic.code field
signals.summary: In the VS Code extension, when a PostToolUse:Edit hook attaches VS Code diagnostics (including markdownlint rules), the extension naively serializes Diagnostic.code via String() coercion. When code is an object (common for markdownlint, which uses {value, target} shape), this produces '[object Object]'. The webview renderer encounters this unknown shape and crashes with a red 'Unhandled case' banner, freezing the chat panel permanently.
aliases: VS Code webview crash object Object markdownlint
Webview freeze on diagnostic object code field
Unhandled case object Object in VS Code extension renderer
signals.review_reason: The webview renderer crashes when processing markdownlint diagnostics with object-typed code fields, freezing the chat panel and requiring 'Reload Window' to recover. This is a session-interrupting event that blocks the user's workflow. Two independent reproductions (different triggers: long markdown edit vs git worktree background servers) confirm the root cause. Any VS Code extension that sets Diagnostic.code as an object (permissive VS Code API behavior) will hit this. Marked P1 because while severe for affected users, it is confined to the VS Code extension.

source_issues.title: Webview crash 'Unhandled case: [object Object]' — markdownlint diagnostics with non-string `code` field
source_issues.evidence: Crash reproducibly triggered by editing a long markdown file with markdownlint enabled. The Diagnostic.code object {value, target} is serialized as [object Object]. The webview reducer enters an unhandled case and renders a crash banner. UI is frozen; only 'Developer: Reload Window' recovers. Issue includes full root-cause analysis and proposed fix.

source_issues.title: [BUG] [BUG] VS Code extension: 'Unhandled case: [object Object]' while reading combined output of two long-running background dev servers (git worktree workflow)
source_issues.evidence: Same webview crash triggered by a different workflow (git worktree + concurrent background processes). Marked as duplicate of #59221. Consistent with the same root cause (Diagnostic.code object serialization failure).

signals.topic: MCP tool calls serialize array/object arguments as JSON strings, violating MCP spec and breaking strict schema validation
signals.summary: When Claude Code calls MCP tools with array or object parameters, the arguments are sent as JSON-encoded strings instead of native types. This breaks any MCP server using standard JSON-schema validation, which is spec-compliant behavior. The root cause is a stray JSON.stringify in @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk.
aliases: MCP tool call array/object arguments wrongly stringified
signals.review_reason: MCP tool calls with array/object parameters are sent as JSON strings instead of native types, breaking any spec-compliant MCP server that validates against its inputSchema. This is a protocol-level violation of the MCP spec and blocks the entire MCP integration workflow for affected servers. The issue includes a fully reproducible test case with a known-good control (mcp-inspector), root-cause trace to @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, and clear user impact (tool calls rejected at validation before reaching user code).

source_issues.title: MCP tool calls: list/dict arguments sent as JSON-encoded strings instead of native arrays/objects
source_issues.evidence: Bug report includes a fully instrumented repro: a Python FastMCP server echoes back argument types. When called via Claude Code, items arrive as python_type=str with value '["a","b"]' instead of list. The same call via @modelcontextprotocol/inspector produces native types, proving the SDK is the culprit. Server-side JSON-schema validation rejects the entire tool call.

signals.topic: Virtiofs mount path permission error bricks Claude Cowork entirely, requiring full Claude Desktop reinstall
signals.summary: When Cowork creates an Artifact, a virtiofs mount path becomes inaccessible (operation not permitted), causing every subsequent Cowork message to fail with an RPC mount error. The error persists across Cowork restarts and sessions, rendering the entire Cowork feature unusable until the user performs a complete reinstall of Claude Desktop.
aliases: Cowork permanently broken after artifact creation
signals.review_reason: This issue renders a primary product feature (Claude Cowork) completely unusable for the affected user, with no in-app recovery. The only fix requires a full Claude Desktop reinstall — a complete product brick scenario. Although only 1 report, the severity is extreme (full feature outage requiring reinstall) and the error is described as reproducible (happened twice). This qualifies as a P0 despite count=1 because the user impact is unambiguous and blocking.

source_issues.title: [BUG] RPC error: failed to mount /mnt/.virtiofs-root/shared/Users... Causes Cowork to break. Complete reinstall needed.
source_issues.evidence: User reports Cowork became completely unresponsive after creating an artifact, throwing 'RPC error: failed to mount ... operation not permitted' on every message. Error persisted across all sessions and restarts. Only resolution was a full uninstall/reinstall of Claude Desktop. Reproduced twice by the user.

signals.topic: Subagent context produces false-positive safety refusals on legitimate academic virology and bioinformatics prompts (viroid, SARS-CoV-2)
signals.summary: Legitimate academic bioinformatics prompts about plant virology (viroid detection from Nanopore sequencing) and SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA are repeatedly refused in subagent context with Usage Policy violations. The same prompts succeed in the main session, indicating a more aggressive classifier in subagent mode. A paying researcher explicitly states they will switch products if unresolved.
aliases: Subagent classifier false positive on virology
Academic bioinformatics prompts refused by subagent safety classifier
Viroid/SARS-CoV-2 prompts blocked only in subagent
signals.review_reason: This issue blocks a paying user from performing core research tasks in the subagent workflow. The user explicitly states intent to cancel the subscription. The false-positive is clearly documented: the same prompts work in the main session, confirming a subagent-specific miscalibration. Request IDs are provided. The safety classifier is over-triggering on standard academic virology terminology (viroids, SARS-CoV-2) that appears in thousands of open-access bioinformatics papers and nf-core pipelines. This is a product-defining trust and accuracy issue.

source_issues.title: False-positive safety refusal blocks legitimate plant-virology and SARS-CoV-2 bioinformatics prompts; same prompts succeed in main session but fail in subagent context
source_issues.evidence: Six consecutive subagent invocations refused on viroid bioinformatics prompts with request IDs provided. Same prompts succeed in main session. User is a paying postdoc researcher at Oregon State University, explicitly states the product is unusable for their core research workflow and they will switch products. SARS-CoV-2 genome analysis prompts also refused. Refusals return in 2-4 seconds indicating an input-side classifier, not response evaluation.

signals.topic: Claude Desktop hardcodes /opt/homebrew/bin/gh path; fails in sandboxed environment with ENOENT
signals.summary: Claude Desktop's GitHub PR manager hardcodes /opt/homebrew/bin/gh as the path to the gh CLI. In the macOS sandbox environment, /opt/homebrew/bin is not accessible, causing spawn ENOENT on every PR polling cycle. This floods the main.log with stack traces, wastes syscall resources, and is suspected to correlate with session instability in large repos with many git worktrees.
aliases: Claude Desktop gh CLI ENOENT in sandbox
GitHub PR checks fail hardcoded path sandbox macOS
signals.review_reason: The gh CLI hardcoded path fails in sandboxed environments (standard macOS App Sandbox), breaking GitHub PR integration for Apple Silicon Homebrew users. The error recurs on a 30s polling cycle, generating hundreds of log entries per session and correlating with session instability events. No in-product workaround; users must aggressively prune git worktrees. This is a clear functional regression that directly breaks a key integration.

source_issues.title: Claude Desktop: gh spawn ENOENT — hardcoded /opt/homebrew path fails in sandbox
source_issues.evidence: User provides full stack traces from main.log showing repeated ENOENT failures. In a repo with 51 worktrees, produced ~328 log entries per session. Worktrees are git's multi-branch checkout feature, commonly used in large projects — suggesting significant real-world exposure. User is paying customer. Root cause confirmed: sandboxed node process cannot access /opt/homebrew/bin regardless of host PATH.

signals.topic: Summarization cookbook fails with BadRequestError due to deprecated assistant message prefill
signals.summary: The summarization cookbook notebook (capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb) crashes with a BadRequestError at cell 8 because it uses assistant message prefill, a deprecated API feature that the model no longer supports. The conversation must end with a user message, but the code prepends an assistant role message, causing the entire notebook tutorial to be unrunnable.
aliases: assistant message prefill deprecation breaks cookbook
summarization notebook broken by API change
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow break: the cookbook notebook is the primary learning asset for summarization capability, and it fails at cell 8 with a 400 error due to a backend API change. Users following the official tutorial cannot complete the summarization example, which is a direct, documented experience failure.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Summarization cookbook fails due to use of assistant message prefill
source_issues.evidence: BadRequestError with error code 400: 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' The notebook is completely unrunnable as a tutorial.

signals.topic: Skills introduction cookbook omits GitHub repo clone as prerequisite, causing onboarding confusion
signals.summary: The skills introduction notebook on the official Claude platform documentation does not mention that users need to clone the claude-cookbooks GitHub repo before following the instructions. The first step says 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' but never tells users where to get that directory. This causes user frustration during onboarding.
aliases: cookbook onboarding missing repo clone step
signals.review_reason: Onboarding friction is a real user experience degradation, though not a workflow-blocking crash. The issue is documented with a specific user experience report of frustration, affecting the official skills introduction tutorial. Count=1 and single-repo scope make P2 appropriate.

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: User reports following the official platform.claude.com cookbook tutorial and getting stuck because the prerequisites section never mentions cloning the GitHub repo. The path '/path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' is referenced without context.

signals.summary: Plugins that are marked as Published in the submission portal are not appearing in the marketplace directory or at claude.com/plugins, making them undiscoverable and un-installable by end users.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocker affecting 4 separate plugin submissions (Magician, agent-handoff x2, Meta VR). Plugins cannot be installed by users despite being marked as Published. The core plugin discovery and installation workflow is completely broken — this is the primary value proposition of the marketplace.

source_issues.title: Published plugin "Magician" not visible for weeks following post-publish
source_issues.evidence: Plugin 'Magician' has state as 'Published' since April 17th but is still not available and not visible as part of official plugin page at claude.com/plugins. Users cannot find or install the plugin despite published status.

source_issues.title: Meta VR plugin not listed after marked as published
source_issues.evidence: Meta VR plugin submitted April 30, 2026 with status flipped to Published two days ago, but has not appeared in this repository or marketplace directory.

signals.topic: code-review plugin documentation inconsistencies (internal repo name exposure, emoji instruction contradiction, version/author metadata drift)

Issues include: information disclosure (internal repo name), conflicting model instructions (emoji), and metadata drift (version/author). Lower priority than functional blockers but worth addressing for plugin quality and trust.

source_issues.title: Doc: code-review link example uses `anthropics/claude-cli-internal` — internal-looking repo name in a public plugin

Author identity contradicts between README (Boris Cherny) and manifest ('Anthropic'). Metadata drift causes downstream tracking issues.

signals.topic: skill-creator: skill packaging and description optimization tools crash or produce zero usable output on Windows
signals.summary: skill-creator scripts crash on Windows due to emoji/encoding issues, and the description optimizer flow produces zero usable output while wasting 300-900K tokens per iteration.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocker for Windows users — package_skill.py crashes on first use, and the description optimizer wastes massive token quota (300-900K per iteration) while producing zero usable output. Affects both skill packaging and optimization core workflows.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: package_skill.py crashes on Windows (emoji print + cp1252 stdout)
source_issues.evidence: scripts/package_skill.py crashes on Windows with UnicodeEncodeError because it prints emoji characters using stdout's default encoding (cp1252 on Windows). Users hit this on first try following documented steps in SKILL.md — no workaround mentioned in docs.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop.py / run_eval.py description optimizer is non-functional on Windows (5 distinct bugs + recall=0% even after compat patches)
source_issues.evidence: 5 distinct Windows compatibility bugs in skill description optimizer flow. Each iteration burns 300-900K tokens with zero usable signal (recall=0%). User's subscription quota wasted on non-functional output. Bugs: cp1252 codec, UTF-8 BOM, claude.CMD not found, select.select on pipes, permission prompts.

signals.topic: security-guidance PreToolUse hook silently fails when plugin root path contains spaces
signals.summary: Hook errors silently on every Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool call when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT path contains a space, affecting Windows usernames and macOS sandboxed HOME paths.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocker — security-guidance hook silently fails on every Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool call. Affects both Windows (common with usernames containing spaces) and macOS (sandboxed sessions). Users believe security reminders are active when they silently fail, creating a false sense of safety.

source_issues.title: security-guidance: PreToolUse hook fails on Windows when ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} expands to a path containing spaces
source_issues.evidence: Hook errors silently on every Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool call when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT path contains a space (common on Windows with usernames like 'Catalin Teodorescu'). Python receives truncated path.

source_issues.title: Unquoted ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in security-guidance hook command breaks when path contains a space
source_issues.evidence: Unquoted shell variable expansion fails on macOS when HOME contains a space (common with '~/Library/Application Support/<app>/...' sandboxed sessions). Every Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool call fails silently.

signals.topic: hookify relative glob silently disables all enforcement rules when plugin hook CWD differs from project root
signals.summary: Hookify rules are silently never loaded when the plugin hook script runs from a CWD other than project root, causing pre-existing enforcement rules to be dead for weeks without user knowledge.
signals.review_reason: Worst-case failure mode for an enforcement tool — users write rules expecting enforcement, rules statically validate, but the harness never sees them. Reporter had 4 rules silently dead for weeks with writes proceeding unblocked. Silent failure mode means users have no indication rules are inactive.

source_issues.title: hookify: relative glob in config_loader.py makes rules silently dead when plugin hook CWD ≠ project root
source_issues.evidence: Hookify rules silently never loaded when plugin hook script runs from CWD other than project root. Reporter had 4 pre-existing enforcement rules silently dead for weeks. Verified that Write tool that should have been blocked actually proceeded. Hookify's failure-mode defaults to 'allow everything' so zero matches silently allows all operations.

signals.topic: README broken link blocks user access to browser-tools-api-demo quickstart

source_issues.title: Documentation: Broken link in README

signals.topic: xlsx/recalc.py 在 Windows 上因 AttributeError 崩溃，核心重算功能不可用

source_issues.title: xlsx recalc.py crashes on Windows: unguarded socket.AF_UNIX access
source_issues.evidence: 完整堆栈、复现环境(Win11+Python 3.14.4 uv)、根因定位(_needs_shim 仅捕获 OSError 不捕获 AttributeError)、已验证的变通方案(直接调用 soffice)。确认影响 xlsx 核心重算功能。

shell mangles multi-byte UTF-8 in docx skill

source_issues.title: v1.34.0 requires libc6 2.38
source_issues.evidence: App fails to start on Ubuntu 22.04 (libc6 2.35) with 'version GLIBC_2.38 not found'. Will also break Debian 12 and RHEL 8/9 which are still supported. Caused by switch to Ubuntu 24.04 build runners in PR #9075.

signals.topic: deepseek-v4-pro with thinking mode fails multi-turn tool calls with HTTP 400
signals.summary: On the tool-result return turn, API returns 400 'reasoning_content must be passed back to the API'. Root cause: Goose strips reasoning_content from assistant messages.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for deepseek-v4-pro users with thinking mode enabled - tool calls fail immediately with hard 400 error on first tool-result turn. No workaround available makes the feature unusable.

source_issues.title: deepseek-v4-pro (thinking mode): multi-turn tool calls fail with 400 "reasoning_content must be passed back to the API"
source_issues.evidence: On the turn where tool result is returned to the model, API returns 400 error: 'reasoning_content must be passed back to the API'. Root cause: Goose strips reasoning_content from assistant messages when constructing next API request. No workaround - user must disable reasoning mode or tool-calling entirely.

signals.topic: Agent cache silently skips custom tool calls during record and replay, breaking replay functionality for workflows that depend on custom tools
signals.summary: When agent caching is enabled, custom tools (passed via the `tools` option) are neither recorded in the cache nor replayed. This causes agent replay to fail for workflows that rely on custom tools for essential actions such as credential-based form filling, silently producing incomplete or broken results without any error indication.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional gap where agent cache silently skips custom tool calls during both recording and replay. The cache records surrounding actions but silently omits custom tool executions, causing replay to produce broken/incomplete results with no error signal. The user has identified the exact root cause in source code and the impact is clearly demonstrated (form filling with credentials fails on replay). While count=1 prevents P0, the impact is non-trivial: essential workflow steps are silently dropped, which is a meaningful experience degradation for anyone using caching with custom tools.

source_issues.title: Agent cache does not record or replay custom tool calls
source_issues.evidence: User traced the root cause in source code: v3CuaAgentHandler.ts does not call recordAgentReplayStep() for custom_tool case; AgentCache.ts executeAgentReplayStep() has no handler for custom_tool and falls through to default skip behavior. Replay silently skips custom tool calls, causing login/credential-filling to fail during replay with no error.

signals.topic: mergeMessages 未去重导致 React duplicate-key 警告
signals.summary: 前端 mergeMessages 函数在合并 historyMessages 和 threadMessages 时未对重复消息 ID 去重，导致每次对话都产生大量 React duplicate-key console 警告，影响开发体验并在生产环境暴露渲染风险。
signals.review_reason: 三条 issue 均指向同一个根因：frontend/src/core/threads/hooks.ts 中 mergeMessages 函数不对合并结果去重。issue #2961 有完整根因分析、修复方案和本地验证；issue #2957 补充了中断会话重新打开的另一种触发场景；issue #2965 的上下文压缩问题中也涉及相同代码路径。count=3，三条独立 issue 均提供了用户可感知的 console 警告作为直接证据，属于明确的 UI 交互问题，P1 优先级。

source_issues.title: fix(frontend): React duplicate-key warnings on chat message list (regression of #655 in v2.0)
source_issues.evidence: v2.0 重写后前端丢失了 v1.x #655 的去重逻辑；单个对话回合产生约 15 条 warning，DevTools 显示红标；提供了完整的修复代码和本地验证结果；根因为 mergeMessages 不对结果去重，LangGraph messages-tuple delta 累加导致同一 id 出现多次

source_issues.title: [runtime] Duplicate React keys when reopening interrupted agent creation session

signals.topic: 沙盒专用工具路径校验逻辑不一致，符号链接场景下 Permission denied
signals.summary: read_file、ls、grep、glob 等专用工具使用 Path.resolve() 进行路径校验，会跟随符号链接导致真实路径超出工作区白名单，而 bash 命令通过字符串替换绕过了相同校验逻辑，造成同一路径下工具行为不一致。
aliases: dedicated tools fail on symlinked paths
signals.review_reason: issue #2934 已 closed，提供了量化对比数据（符号链接 vs 硬链接场景下专用工具效率 53.3% vs 100%），明确指出根因代码位置和不对称校验逻辑，并揭示了级联影响：工具失效 → bash fallback → 更多 turn 消耗 → 递归限制 → 假阳性循环检测。虽然 count=1，但影响程度大（有实验数据支撑），且涉及 SWE-bench 等核心评测场景，影响主流程任务完成率，P1 优先级合理。

source_issues.title: fix: Asymmetric path validation in sandbox tools causes dedicated tools to fail on symlinked repos
source_issues.evidence: 提供了对比数据：符号链接时 bash 占比 35.7%（工具不可用导致 fallback），硬链接时 bash 占比 0%（工具正常）；根因明确为 backend/packages/harness/deerflow/sandbox/tools.py 中专用工具走 _resolve_and_validate_user_data_path() 而 bash 走 replace_virtual_paths_in_command() 的不对称逻辑；cascade 导致更多 turn 消耗、递归限制和假阳性循环检测

signals.topic: PostgreSQL 模式下 journal flush 失败：FOR UPDATE 不支持聚合函数
signals.summary: 配置 PostgreSQL 时，journal flush 阶段执行 select(max(seq)) with FOR UPDATE 触发 asyncpg.FeatureNotSupportedError: FOR UPDATE is not allowed with aggregate functions，导致 run 的 journal 无法持久化，每次对话均有 WARNING 日志。
signals.review_reason: 完整 stack trace 指向具体代码行，错误为 PostgreSQL asyncpg 的已知限制（FOR UPDATE 禁止用于聚合函数），每次 run 结束都触发 WARNING 导致 journal 持久化不可靠。count=1 但有明确 DB 报错和完整堆栈，数据库持久化失败属于主流程阻断性问题，P1 优先级。

source_issues.title: database配置为PostgreSQL，对话过程中日志报错：FOR UPDATE is not allowed with aggregate functions
source_issues.evidence: 完整 stack trace 显示 asyncpg.exceptions.FeatureNotSupportedError；根因位于 backend/packages/harness/deerflow/runtime/events/store/db.py:132 的 put_batch 方法，select(func.max(RunEventRow.seq)).with_for_update() 在 PostgreSQL asyncpg 中不被支持；每次对话 run 结束后均触发 WARNING，影响 journal 持久化可靠性

signals.topic: 子代理上报 token 使用量时 callback 类型错误导致崩溃退出
signals.summary: 子代理在获取 token 使用量 recorder 时，从 runtime.config 获取的 callbacks 类型从 list 变成了 LangChain AsyncCallbackManager 对象，for 循环遍历时触发 TypeError，导致子代理直接退出。
signals.review_reason: 子代理运行过程中因 callback 类型不匹配直接崩溃退出，导致 run 流程中断，属于主流程阻断性问题。截图和函数分析均指向 _find_usage_recorder 的类型处理缺陷，count=1 但有截图证据和代码分析，P1 优先级。

source_issues.title: [Bug] 子代理上报token使用情况时获取callback异常，导致子代理退出
source_issues.evidence: 函数 _find_usage_recorder 从 runtime.config 获取 callbacks 进行遍历，但此时 callbacks 已不是 list 类型而是 LangChain 的 AsyncCallbackManager 对象；for cb in callbacks: 触发 TypeError；子代理直接退出，run 流程中断

signals.topic: CLI v3.0.x: AWS Bedrock profile authentication completely broken — region/credentials not passed to AI SDK
signals.summary: CLI 3.0.2 silently drops the `options` field (region, profile, credentials) when constructing GatewayProviderConfig, causing every AWS Bedrock request to fail with 'AWS region setting is missing'. VS Code extension unaffected. Multiple users confirm downgrade to 2.18.0 fixes it.
aliases: AWS Bedrock CLI profile auth broken
Bedrock credentials not passed to AI SDK
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed reports with identical error message 'AWS region setting is missing', root cause traced to missing `options` field in GatewayProviderConfig in handler-factory.ts. VS Code extension unaffected — this is a CLI-only regression introduced in 3.0.x that completely blocks AWS Bedrock usage in CLI.

source_issues.title: AWS Bedrock profile authentication broken in CLI 3.0.2
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in handler-factory.ts: options field is missing from GatewayProviderConfig. CLI fails even when all AWS config (region, profile, credentials) is properly set.

source_issues.title: Allow other AWS Bedrock connection methods in latest CLI version not only API Key
source_issues.evidence: CLI 3.0.2 cannot use profile-based AWS credentials. 'Use existing configuration' shows no models and returns forbidden on chat.

source_issues.title: Error: AWS region setting is missing. Pass it using the 'region' parameter or the AWS_REGION environment variable.
source_issues.evidence: Immediately reproduces on upgrade from 2.18.0. Downgrade restores functionality. Auto-update triggers regression.

signals.topic: CLI v3.0.x: OpenAI-compatible endpoint setup fails with 'Unknown or disabled provider "openai"' — breaks BYOK flow
signals.summary: Setting up a custom OpenAI-compatible provider (e.g., vLLM) through the CLI TUI results in an 'Unknown or disabled provider' error when attempting to send messages. Auto-update from 2.18.0 also triggers the same error. VS Code extension works fine with the same configuration.
signals.review_reason: 2 reports (10750 and 10741) both confirm 'Unknown or disabled provider openai' error in CLI when using OpenAI-compatible endpoints. 10750 includes TUI reproduction steps. The auto-update path (10741) shows this is a CLI v3.0.x regression. While count=2, the BYOK (bring-your-own-provider) flow is a core product feature — its breakage in CLI is a significant experience gap vs VS Code extension.

source_issues.title: Error: Unknown or disabled provider "openai".
source_issues.evidence: User sets up OpenAI-compatible endpoint via TUI ('Bring your own provider' -> 'OpenAI Compatible' -> API Key -> model ID). Error occurs on first message send. Same config works in VSCode extension.

source_issues.title: How to disable auto-update in Cline CLI? Multiple issues with v2.18.0
source_issues.evidence: After auto-update to 3.0.2, OpenAI-compatible API provider fails with 'Unknown or disabled provider openai' — was working before update.

signals.topic: VSCode/JetBrains: MiniMax provider returns 401 authentication error even with valid API key
signals.summary: MiniMax provider returns 401 'login fail: Please carry the API secret key in the X-Api-Key field' error. The user has a valid MiniMax key but Cline appears to be sending credentials incorrectly, causing all MiniMax LLM calls to fail.
signals.review_reason: Clear user impact: every MiniMax model call fails with 401 auth error despite valid credentials. Cline is likely sending the key in the wrong header format (standard Authorization header vs MiniMax's required X-Api-Key header). Affects core provider integration.

source_issues.title: [Windows specific] MiniMax AI Provider: invalid x-api-key is shown when trying to use any minimax LLM
source_issues.evidence: User provides valid MiniMax API key (sk-cp-...). Cline returns 401 with message 'Please carry the API secret key in the X-Api-Key field of the request header'. Affects all MiniMax models.

signals.topic: VSCode/JetBrains: Cerebras provider rejects tool calls with 'effort' and 'reasoningSummary' — models generate unsupported fields
signals.summary: Cerebras models (zai-glm-4.7, gpt-oss-120b) generate tool calls that include 'effort' and 'reasoningSummary' properties, but Cline's Cerebras provider schema rejects these as unsupported, causing every request to fail.
signals.review_reason: Explicit schema validation errors prevent any Cerebras model from functioning. The model generates properties that the provider rejects, creating a complete block for Cerebras users.

source_issues.title: Cerebras Provider: "effort: property 'effort' is unsupported reasoningSummary: property 'reasoningSummary' is unsupported..." error is shown when trying to run prompt using zai-glm-4.7 and gpt-oss-120b LLM

signals.topic: CLI: SSO session does not persist across agent launches — forces re-authentication every time
signals.summary: CLI users with SSO-based sign-in must re-authenticate on every terminal session. Auth session and provider configuration are not persisted, breaking the CLI workflow. VS Code extension handles this correctly.
signals.review_reason: SSO session persistence failure forces repeated re-authentication, degrading the CLI from a persistent agent to a session-by-session tool. This is a clear workflow interruption.

source_issues.title: SSO session doesn't persist on each agent launch
source_issues.evidence: User with SSO sign-in sees authentication screen on every terminal session. Provider configuration not persisted between launches. VS Code extension works correctly.

signals.topic: PowerShell Core scripts fail at runtime on Windows due to hardcoded legacy powershell.exe
signals.summary: When Continue executes terminal commands on Windows, it hardcodes powershell.exe (PowerShell 5.1) instead of preferring PowerShell Core (pwsh 6+). Modern PowerShell scripts with features like ternary operators, pipeline chain operators, or non-ASCII characters fail in legacy PowerShell, causing unpredictable errors and silent Unicode data corruption — with no user workaround.
aliases: powershell.exe vs pwsh version mismatch on Windows
signals.review_reason: Count=1 but review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: complete workflow failure for any user running modern PowerShell scripts, silent Unicode data corruption with no user workaround, hardcoded invocation bypasses user system configuration. Single-issue threshold met because evidence demonstrates a systemic code defect (hardcoded binary path) that universally affects all Windows users who use PowerShell Core.

source_issues.title: Hardcoded legacy Windows PowerShell (powershell.exe) causes runtime failures and degraded UX
source_issues.evidence: Scripts with modern PowerShell syntax (ternary operators, &&/|| pipeline chains) fail with syntax errors. Unicode handling in legacy PowerShell silently replaces non-ASCII chars with '?', corrupting filenames, prices, and config values. The user explicitly states 'this issue is entirely uncorrectable by the end user' because the invocation is hardcoded.

signals.topic: Autocomplete repeatedly calls wrong model name "AUTODETECT" instead of configured model
signals.summary: Continue's autocomplete feature continuously calls a literal "AUTODETECT" model identifier instead of the user's configured model, causing repeated API failures and wasted requests.
signals.review_reason: Autocomplete is a core, frequently-used feature. The bug causes the system to call a literal placeholder model name instead of the configured model, producing repeated API failures. Multiple Blablador users confirmed being affected, establishing clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Continue keeps calling "AUTODETECT" model
source_issues.evidence: Multiple Blablador users are actively hitting this issue. Autocomplete is a core feature; calling a literal 'AUTODETECT' string as a model name will result in API failures against any real provider.

signals.topic: Autocomplete returns completely wrong suggestions for large files (>3000 lines) in JetBrains IDE due to incorrect prefix/suffix context extraction
signals.summary: On JetBrains IDE (Linux), autocomplete for files over ~3000 lines extracts wrong prefix and suffix context, causing suggestions that are totally irrelevant regardless of cursor position. The VS Code plugin works correctly with the same config, confirming this is a JetBrains-specific regression.
aliases: wrong prefix suffix context autocomplete JetBrains
signals.review_reason: Autocomplete is a core feature. For large files (a common real-world scenario), suggestions are completely wrong and stale, making the feature actively harmful rather than helpful. Confirmed by log evidence and cross-IDE comparison showing VS Code works fine.

source_issues.title: Truncated / wrong prefix & suffix on large file Autocompletion
source_issues.evidence: User provides prompt.log files showing correct prefix/suffix for small files but identical wrong prefix/suffix for large files regardless of cursor position. VS Code plugin works correctly with the same config, isolating the bug to the JetBrains integration.

signals.topic: All terminal commands fail immediately for tcsh/csh users due to hardcoded login shell flag
signals.summary: Continue hardcodes the `-l` flag when launching Unix shells. tcsh and csh do not support `-l`, causing every terminal command to fail with 'Unknown option: `-l`' regardless of what command is being run.
signals.review_reason: Terminal tool execution is a core workflow feature. For tcsh/csh users (non-trivial shell family), every command fails with exit code 1, completely blocking the terminal tool. Exact error log provided; root cause is a single hardcoded flag that is not conditionally applied based on shell type.

source_issues.title: Terminal commands fail when `$SHELL` is set to `tcsh` due to hardcoded `-l` shell flag
source_issues.evidence: Every terminal command fails with 'Unknown option: `-l`' for any user with $SHELL=/bin/tcsh. Basic commands like pwd, ls -a, echo hello all fail. Exit code 1 on all commands means terminal tool functionality is completely broken for this shell family.

signals.topic: PR checks re-post stale results on new commits instead of re-evaluating, creating misleading CI feedback for hours
signals.summary: When a PR is updated (new commits pushed), Continue re-posts the original PR-open check task IDs as statuses on the new head commits instead of creating fresh agent sessions. This makes stale results appear as live check results, wasting hours of debugging time.
aliases: stale PR check status on new commits
check agent session not refreshed on PR synchronize
signals.review_reason: PR checks are a documented core product feature used seriously as a CI feedback signal. Stale task IDs produce misleading CI results that persist for hours, consuming significant debugging time. Detailed evidence with actual task IDs and timestamps confirms the systemic nature of the issue.

source_issues.title: PR checks do not create fresh agent sessions on PR updates; stale task IDs re-post to new commits
source_issues.evidence: Detailed evidence: same 3 task IDs re-used across 6 PR head commits. No new agent sessions observed after PR open. A fix commit was pushed and task IDs remained identical, with task diff=null. CI status stayed failed for ~6 hours despite remediation attempts. User was forced to push an empty commit trying to trigger re-evaluation.

signals.topic: ValkeyStorage metadata_filter silently returns wrong results or errors
signals.summary: Issue 5795 shows metadata_filter clauses reference arbitrary metadata key fields but the Valkey FT schema only defines VectorField, TagField(scope), TagField(categories), NumericField(created_at), NumericField(importance). FT.SEARCH with custom metadata_filter will either error or silently return wrong results, corrupting knowledge retrieval.
signals.review_reason: Schema mismatch between user-defined metadata_filter fields and Valkey FT index schema causes silent wrong results or errors in knowledge retrieval. Affects correctness of RAG workflows relying on ValkeyStorage metadata filtering.

source_issues.title: metadata_filter with Valkey storage leads to error or wrong result
source_issues.evidence: metadata_filter references arbitrary keys but Valkey FT schema only has fixed fields. FT.SEARCH will error or silently return wrong results, corrupting knowledge retrieval.

signals.topic: Tool retry causes duplicate side effects (no idempotency guard)
signals.summary: When a task fails and retries, any @tool decorated function that already executed runs again with no mechanism to detect completion. Issue 5802 provides concrete evidence: duplicate payments, emails, and trades are possible when external API calls are retried. The user shows a real code example and references LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 confirming the same failure pattern in production. This is a main-flow blocking issue for any user running agents with paid side effects.
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking for users with paid side effects. Concrete evidence of duplicate payments/emails/trades on retry. References same failure pattern confirmed in LangGraph Cloud production (issue #7417). Strong user impact despite single issue count.

source_issues.title: agents and tools are running twice on error
source_issues.evidence: User reports tools/agents run twice on error. Provides real code example showing duplicate payments, emails, trades possible on retry. References LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 showing same pattern in production.

signals.topic: OPENAI_API_KEY env var not propagated to subprocess execution context
signals.summary: Issue 5622 shows the API key works via curl/Python but fails inside CrewAI subprocess with 401 invalid_api_key. The error log shows VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch warning and the API key being passed but failing. This is a main-flow blocker for users trying to run CrewAI in containerized environments where environment variable propagation across subprocess boundaries is required.
aliases: env var not passed to subprocess
signals.review_reason: API key works in main process but fails inside subprocess with 401, blocking the entire agent execution flow. Critical for containerized/CI deployments where subprocess env propagation is required. Strong user impact evidence despite count=1.

source_issues.title: OPENAI_API_KEY env variable not working for crewAI subprocess
source_issues.evidence: API key works in curl/Python but fails inside CrewAI subprocess with 401 invalid_api_key. Error log shows VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch. Main flow blocked for containerized deployments.

signals.topic: HITL pre-review silently falls back to raw output on any exception
signals.summary: Issue 5725 documents that when human_feedback with learn=True encounters an exception (network, auth, LLM, or structured-output failure), _pre_review_with_lessons catches all exceptions and returns the original method_output with no warning or error logged. This creates invisible bypass of the human-in-the-loop safeguard.
signals.review_reason: HITL safeguard silently bypassed on any exception (network, auth, LLM, or structured-output failure), giving users false confidence that human review is active when it is not. Trust/correctness impact for safety-critical workflows.

source_issues.title: human in the loop learning: _pre_review_with_lessons raises exception if Learn is set to True
source_issues.evidence: _pre_review_with_lessons silently catches all exceptions and returns original output with no warning. Downstream cannot distinguish pre-reviewed from raw output. Human safeguard appears active but is actually bypassed.

signals.topic: Knowledge metadata filtering not configurable via KnowledgeConfig / Crew.query_knowledge
signals.summary: Issue 5805 documents 4 gaps: KnowledgeConfig lacks metadata_filter field, Knowledge.query() drops metadata_filter silently, Crew.query_knowledge() lacks metadata_filter param, and BaseKnowledgeSource self.metadata is never written to vector store documents. User-facing API does not expose metadata filtering available in lower layers.
signals.review_reason: Core RAG metadata filtering feature is broken across all API layers despite underlying storage support. Users cannot filter knowledge by metadata in production workflows.

source_issues.title: Knowledge metadata filtering not working / missing
source_issues.evidence: 4 specific gaps identified: KnowledgeConfig missing field, query() drops filter, Crew.query_knowledge lacks param, BaseKnowledgeSource.metadata never persisted. Lower layers support it but top-level API does not expose it.

In issue #27031 the agent stalls mid-conversation and requires model switching as a workaround; in #27036 the thinking state never resolves. This is a clear P0: high-frequency (4 reports), directly blocks the primary interactive workflow, and is confirmed across multiple users and environments.

source_issues.title: 一直处于思考阶段，问答没有响应和输出
source_issues.evidence: CLI runs but user gets no response — repeatedly stuck in 'thinking' state regardless of working directory. Screenshot attached showing permanent thinking state with no output.

source_issues.title: Auto (gemini 3) stalls at 'thinking'
source_issues.evidence: Agent stops responding mid-conversation. Prompts get stuck on 'thinking' for minutes. Switching models temporarily resolves it, switching back causes it again. Chat history attached. Session ID logged.

source_issues.title: Thinking are buggy after > 0.41.1 release
source_issues.evidence: Thinking logic broken after 0.41.2 release, working fine in 0.41.1. Takes longer to process and receive response. Multiple comments confirm regression.

source_issues.title: GeminiCLI.com Feedback: [ISSUE]
source_issues.evidence: After latest update, CLI chat repeatedly stuck in thinking state with no response. Screenshot attached showing unresolvable thinking state. User explicitly requesting solution.

signals.topic: Pro/Ultra subscription tier not recognized — paying users placed on free-tier quotas
signals.summary: Paid Google One AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers report that the CLI shows incorrect tier (Google Assist instead of Pro/Ultra) and enforces free-tier request limits (200/day) instead of their entitled quotas (1500/day), causing workflow disruption and legal threats.
signals.review_reason: Direct cost/billing impact for paying subscribers. Two distinct users with active Pro/Ultra subscriptions are blocked from using their entitled features and quotas. Issue #27043 involves a user threatening legal action and being unable to use the CLI properly since March 2024 — this is a persistent, high-impact failure of entitlement recognition. The P0 threshold is met via strong user impact evidence (billing fraud concern, legal threat, confirmed active subscription with wrong quotas enforced).

source_issues.title: Pro limits not honored -Same issue with antigravity
source_issues.evidence: CLI shows 'Gemini Code Assist in Google One AI Pro' tier but enforces 200 req/day (free-tier) instead of 1500 req/day. After only 36 requests, usage shows ~18%. User has active Google One subscription verified. User states 'I believe that's my last try before taking legal action.' Antigravity IDE also broken by same subscription issue.
