signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：skill publish和new version upload是publisher核心操作，被同一个Convex server error阻塞。2个独立用户在不同入口点（publish页面、new version按钮）触发同一错误，均提供了Request ID证据。阻塞时间持续6小时以上，反复失败。P1优先级。

source_issues.title: [CONVEX Q(skills:checkSlugAvailability)] Server Error when updating skill
source_issues.evidence: User attempted to publish skill with slug `chess-with-claw`. Error: 'Something went wrong [CONVEX Q(skills:checkSlugAvailability)] [Request ID: 733d42dc27711e86] Server Error Called by client'. signals.topic: Aider crashes on startup due to long CLI arguments exceeding OS argv length limit
signals.summary: When users pass long values (e.g., --system-prompt, --system-prompt-prefix, --custom-instruction) as CLI arguments, Python's argv list hits the OS-imposed limit (ARG_MAX), causing an uncaught OSError (errno 63 'File name too long') in pathlib.py during initial stat() calls. This is a complete blocker — users cannot launch aider at all when using long custom instructions or system prompts via CLI flags.
aliases: OSError file name too long startup crash
signals.review_reason: 3 distinct users on both macOS and unspecified platforms experience a complete startup crash (aider fails to launch) when using long custom instruction values via CLI flags. The crash is uncaught and unhandled, making this a hard blocker for any user who has detailed system prompts or custom instructions. The root cause (OS argv length limit exceeded) is confirmed by the errno 63 in pathlib.stat().

signals.topic: TokenBucketRateLimiter/SlidingWindowRateLimiter async_acquire() blocks the asyncio event loop due to threading.Lock

aliases: asyncio event loop blocking in rate limiter
async rate limiter blocks event loop
signals.review_reason: This is a critical async runtime bug that blocks the event loop thread with blocking syscalls. The provided reproducer empirically demonstrates 200-400ms freezes during normal async pipeline operations. All async LLM and embedding pipelines using the built-in rate limiter are affected, representing a main-flow performance collapse. No workaround available to users.

OpenTelemetry orphan spans in sync tools

OpenTelemetry users relying on ContextVar for distributed tracing will get broken span trees (orphaned spans) for every sync FunctionTool call. The bug is confirmed by the reporter with a test reproducer and affects any user using sync tools with instrumentation packages. It was closed without a fix being merged, leaving the bug unaddressed.

signals.topic: IndexNode obj field serialization broken after migration from .dict() to model_dump()
signals.summary: PR #18447 replaced node.dict() with node.model_dump() in serialization paths. Deserialization via metadata_dict_to_node() and IndexNode.from_dict() (via json_to_doc()) expects the __type__ wrapper and throws, silently replacing IndexNode.obj with a backup TextNode.
aliases: model_dump vs dict serialization mismatch for IndexNode
signals.review_reason: This is a silent data loss bug in a core data serialization path. signals.topic: memory search returns 0 results on fresh install: schema hardcodes 768-dim but default embedding model is 384-dim
signals.summary: After a clean install with the default embedding model (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim), ruflo memory search always returns 0 results. The schema creates 768-dim vector indexes but the default model produces 384-dim vectors, causing HNSW to reject all indexed vectors. This affects default CLI usage, Windows environments, and Bridge-imported embeddings. This is the headline feature of the product and it is broken out of the box.
aliases: embedding dimension mismatch causes memory search to return zero results
memory search broken on default install
signals.review_reason: This is a core product feature (semantic memory search) that is broken on the default fresh install. All four issues share the same root cause: vector embedding dimension mismatch between the hardcoded schema (768-dim) and the default embedding model (384-dim). Users who run 'ruflo init --full' get a memory system that silently returns zero results — they see success messages but no actual search functionality. This is a main-flow failure with clear user impact: the headline feature does not work.

source_issues.title: memory search returns 0 results on default install: schema is 768-dim but default model is 384-dim
source_issues.evidence: Clean install with default model always returns 0 results. Three compounding bugs: schema hardcodes 768-dim, entries stored in wrong namespace, default threshold too aggressive. Reproduction steps provided with actual 0-result output.

source_issues.title: Windows: memory store succeeds but search returns no results and stats shows 0 entries (v3.7.0-alpha.27)
source_issues.evidence: Verified on Windows 11. Store prints success + entry ID, but search returns 'No results found' and stats shows 'Total Entries: 0'. Reproduced with upsert/ttl/tags and after daemon restart.

source_issues.title: Bridge search index uses 768-dim while imported embeddings are 384-dim
source_issues.evidence: 110 of 111 imported rows use 384-dim embeddings but vector index is configured for 768-dim. Namespace search remains broken even if HNSW index is provisioned.

source_issues.evidence: memory stats reads from .claude/memory.db while memory store/search write to .swarm/memory.db. Reports HNSW '0 entries' even when data has just been stored and retrieved via semantic search. Data is fine but the stats command is reading the wrong file.

signals.topic: CLI memory commands report success but do not persist data across invocations — false-success and silent data loss
signals.summary: ruflo memory store (and retrieve/list/search/stats) report success but never share state across CLI invocations because each invocation spawns a fresh sql.js process. The MCP daemon path works correctly, but the CLI surface gives users false-success messages and silent data loss. ruflo doctor also incorrectly reports the database as uninitialized when it exists on disk.
aliases: CLI memory store false success no persistence
ruflo doctor false positive memory not initialized
sql.js fresh process per CLI invocation memory not persisted
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues all describe the same underlying defect: CLI memory operations report success without persisting data. This is a false-success pattern — the user believes their data was stored, but it vanishes on the next invocation. Combined with ruflo doctor giving contradictory diagnostics, users cannot trust the CLI at all for memory operations. This is a main-flow failure affecting core memory functionality.

source_issues.title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] CLI memory store reports success but does not persist — fresh sql.js process per invocation (MCP path works correctly)
source_issues.evidence: CLI commands report success but never share state across invocations. Store command prints success + entry ID, but subsequent retrieve/search/stats commands show 0 entries. MCP daemon path works correctly. Users receive false-success messages and silent data loss.

source_issues.evidence: ruflo doctor reports warning even though memory.db exists on disk with the full ruflo schema and the MCP daemon is reading/writing it successfully. Misleading diagnostic that compounds the persistence confusion.

source_issues.title: Windows: memory store succeeds but search returns no results and stats shows 0 entries (v3.7.0-alpha.27)
source_issues.evidence: On Windows 11: store prints success + entry ID, search prints 'No results found', stats shows 'Total Entries: 0'. Reproduced with upsert/ttl/tags and after daemon restart. Additional assertion failure on UV_HANDLE_CLOSING when re-running memory init.

signals.topic: Hook scaffolding writes project-anchored paths but installs helper scripts globally — every Bash/Edit/Session hook fires MODULE_NOT_FOUND
signals.summary: ruflo init writes hook commands anchored at $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/helpers/... in settings.json, but the installer only deposits helper scripts under ~/.claude/helpers/ (global). Result: every Bash/Edit/Session hook fires MODULE_NOT_FOUND in every project the user opens. Additionally, hook-handler.cjs falls back to a raw object for the prompt, causing a TypeError on every pre-bash invocation from Claude Code.
aliases: hook scaffolding path mismatch global vs project install
hook handler TypeError on every bash call
signals.review_reason: Three compounding issues break the hook system completely: (1) path mismatch causes MODULE_NOT_FOUND on every hook in every project immediately after init, (2) a TypeError fires on every pre-bash call once hooks partially work, and (3) stop hooks fail with TLS errors on session end, surfacing errors to users repeatedly. The hook system is advertised as a core extensibility mechanism and is completely broken out of the box after running 'ruflo init'.

source_issues.title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] Hook scaffolding writes $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR paths but installs helpers globally — every Bash hook MODULE_NOT_FOUND
source_issues.evidence: ruflo init writes hook commands to ~/.claude/settings.json anchored at ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/helpers/..., but the installer only deposits helpers under ~/.claude/helpers/. Every Bash/Edit/Session hook fires MODULE_NOT_FOUND in every project. Visible on every Bash tool call from Claude Code.

source_issues.title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] hook-handler.cjs:116 falls back to toolInput (object) for prompt — pre-bash hook TypeError on every Bash call
source_issues.evidence: hook-handler.cjs line 116 falls back to toolInput (the parsed object) when building prompt, then line 148 calls .toLowerCase() on it. Every pre-bash invocation from Claude Code prints a TypeError warning: '(hookInput.command || prompt).toLowerCase is not a function'.

source_issues.title: Stop hook fails with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE on session-end
source_issues.evidence: Session-end stop hooks fail on Windows because npx cannot reach the npm registry due to TLS certificate verification error. Error is non-blocking but still surfaces to the user every time a session ends.

signals.topic: daemon start --workers flag accepts input but ignores it — always enables all default workers regardless of flag
signals.summary: ruflo daemon start --workers map accepts the flag but the daemon still enables the full default worker set (map, audit, optimize, consolidate, testgaps). Users who want to limit resource usage cannot do so, leading to unnecessary CPU/memory overhead.
aliases: daemon enables all workers regardless of --workers flag
signals.review_reason: The --workers flag is silently ignored, which could cause resource overconsumption. While only 1 issue, the bug is clearly documented with reproduction steps and verified against a specific version. The false-positive flag behavior is a trust-destroying UX issue, though it is non-blocking.

source_issues.title: daemon start --workers map still enables default workers
source_issues.evidence: Verified against v3.7.0-alpha.33. daemon start --workers map accepts the flag but ruflo daemon status shows 5 workers running: map, audit, optimize, consolidate, testgaps. Expected: only 'map' enabled. Reproduction steps and observed output provided.

signals.topic: statusline reads encrypted memory.db as SQLite and displays fabricated metrics (3.3B fake patterns, 100% DDD progress)
signals.summary: When encryption at rest is enabled, statusline.cjs reads bytes 28-31 of the encrypted memory.db and interprets ciphertext as a SQLite page count. This produces garbage values (3.3 billion patterns) that cascade into fake DDD domain counts (5/5) and 100% intelligence metrics, making the statusline silently lie about progress.
aliases: encrypted memory.db read as SQLite produces fake statusline metrics
statusline fabricated progress metrics encryption enabled
signals.review_reason: Single issue but the user impact is clear: the statusline, which is the primary UX feedback mechanism shipped with every init, displays completely fabricated progress metrics when encryption is enabled (the default). Users making decisions based on DDD completion or pattern counts are working with false data. While not flow-blocking, this is a significant UX integrity failure.

source_issues.title: statusline: encrypted memory.db (RFE1) produces 3.3B pattern count, cascades into fake 100% DDD/Neural progress
source_issues.evidence: Encryption at rest (default with recent inits) causes statusline to read ciphertext bytes and interpret them as SQLite page count. Produces 3367093.6k patterns, 5/5 DDD domains, 100% intelligence — all fabricated from garbage uint32. Full forensic evidence and reproduction steps provided.

source_issues.evidence: Chrome crashes immediately on startup inside Docker containers (alpine/openclaw base image) with SIGTRAP/trap int3. Core dumps confirm crash location in chrome binary. Makes agent-browser completely unusable in Docker, which is a primary CI/CD deployment target.

signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: 在 Windows 11 的非 TTY 上下文中 --headed 模式完全不显示浏览器窗口，阻断所有需要可见浏览器窗口的身份验证流程 (OIDC PKCE、人工登录等)。这是 Windows 平台上 AI agent 工作流的核心场景，直接导致 agent-browser 在该环境下无法用于认证驱动的自动化任务。

signals.topic: Proxy environment variables with trailing slash cause ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES, breaking proxy for common third-party tool configurations

source_issues.title: ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES when proxy environment variables contain trailing slash

signals.topic: Page.stopScreencast freezes live preview stream after recording stops, requiring session close to recover
signals.summary: Page.stopScreencast called on record stop freezes the live preview stream for other consumers (cdp_loop.rs stream), requiring session restart to recover.

signals.topic: next/image disk-LRU cache permanently poisoned by a single 0-byte file in .next/cache/images/, breaking all image optimization for the process lifetime
signals.summary: A single 0-byte file placed in .next/cache/images/ (e.g., from a Ctrl-C interrupted `next dev` on Windows) permanently poisons the disk-LRU singleton. The error 'LRUCache: calculateSize returned 0, but size must be > 0' is thrown and every subsequent image optimization request fails, with the process unable to write any new images to cache.
signals.review_reason: Critical image optimization failure. A single corrupt cache entry permanently disables the entire image optimization pipeline for the process lifetime. Common trigger (Ctrl-C on Windows) makes this a real-world user scenario. Not a one-off edge case — this is a cache design vulnerability where one bad entry permanently blocks all subsequent operations.

source_issues.title: next/image: a single 0-byte file in .next/cache/images/ permanently poisons the disk-LRU singleton
source_issues.evidence: A 0-byte file in .next/cache/images/ causes initCacheEntries to push {key, size: 0}, which causes LRUCache.set to throw. The throw escapes the async IIFE, leaving _diskLRUPromise rejected. Every future await getOrInitDiskLRU(...) re-throws — the cache is permanently poisoned for the rest of the process. All image optimization requests fail indefinitely.

signals.topic: Race condition — task completes before subprocess writes declared outputs when descendant processes leave the tracked process group, causing downstream tasks to fail
signals.summary: When a task spawns a subprocess that leaves the tracked process group (via `detached: true`, `setsid`, or `setpgid`), turbo signals task completion immediately after the direct child exits, before grandchild processes finish writing output files. This causes dependent tasks (`^build`-style) to start and fail with "Could not resolve" because the output file is not yet on disk. Reproduced at 99.5-100% race rate in synthetic tests; ~1.2% failure rate in real-world CI.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow failure — builds silently produce incorrect results (outputs not written yet when dependents start) or fail entirely with module-not-found errors. The race is deterministic under common real-world patterns (bunx detached subprocess, double-fork) and has been observed in production CI. It directly undermines turbo's core guarantee of correct task ordering and caching.

source_issues.title: Task signaled complete before subprocess writes declared outputs when descendants leave the tracked process group
source_issues.evidence: User reported 99.5-100% failure rate in synthetic tests and ~1.2% in real Linux CI. Downstream tasks fail with 'Could not resolve' because outputs are not yet written when dependent tasks start. PR #12790 was opened to fix the in-group case. This is a non-deterministic build failure that silently causes wrong cache artifacts.

signals.topic: `turbo prune --docker` fails with `bun install` when package.json contains literal workspace entries
signals.summary: When `workspaces` in package.json uses literal entries (not just globs), `turbo prune --docker` produces an invalid pruned package.json. Running `bun install` in the pruned output then fails with "Workspace not found" for each literal workspace reference, breaking Docker image builds.
aliases: turbo prune bun workspace not found
signals.review_reason: Blocks the entire Docker build pipeline when using bun as package manager with literal workspace entries. The pruned output is invalid and bun install fails, which is a complete build failure for containerized monorepo deployments.

source_issues.title: literal workspaces + `turbo prune --docker` + `bun install` fails
source_issues.evidence: User reported that `bun install` fails with 'Workspace not found' errors in the pruned Docker output when literal workspace entries exist in package.json. This is a Docker build blocker — the pruned artifact is unusable with bun.

signals.topic: SIGINT signal not forwarded when `script-shell=sh` — graceful shutdown fails for Windows users with default shell
signals.summary: When `script-shell=sh` (Windows default), turbo does not forward SIGINT to child processes. This means dev servers and long-running processes do not receive the interrupt signal and cannot trigger their graceful shutdown sequences, leaving zombie processes or forced termination instead of clean shutdown.
signals.review_reason: Affects all Windows users running `turbo start` with the default shell configuration. Graceful shutdown of development servers fails, meaning cleanup logic is skipped and processes are force-killed. This is a persistent, reproducible DX issue that Windows users cannot easily work around without changing shell configs.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` is not forwarded properly when `script-shell=sh`
source_issues.evidence: User demonstrated that with bash shell SIGINT fires and triggers graceful shutdown (shutdown code runs, process exits cleanly). With default sh shell, SIGINT is never received by the child process — no graceful shutdown code runs, process is killed immediately. Affects all Windows users using npm's default shell configuration.

signals.topic: vercel env add silently stores empty string despite reporting success, risking secret rotation
signals.summary: CLI command `vercel env add` reports 'Added Environment Variable' but actually stores an empty string. This silent failure affects all three input patterns (stdin pipe, --value flag, file redirect). Dangerous for secret rotation as credentials silently become empty strings with a green success message.
aliases: vercel env pull returns empty value after env add
signals.review_reason: Critical silent failure on a core CLI operation (environment variable management). Reports success but stores empty string. Directly risks production secrets being silently corrupted — Stripe keys, HMAC tokens, service credentials all vulnerable. High severity with clear user impact evidence: deterministic 100% reproduction, author explicitly describes production outage risk, workaround forces users to dashboard.

source_issues.title: vercel env add reports success but stores empty string (CLI 53.3.2)
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible: all three input patterns (stdin pipe, --value flag, file redirect) result in empty string stored. Author explicitly warns: 'Silent failure on env set is dangerous for secret rotation: Stripe webhook secrets, HMAC keys, service role tokens could all silently rotate to empty string with a green CLI receipt.' Preview env also has a secondary bug (requires --value --yes --force).

signals.topic: vercel logs pagination returns duplicate entries beyond 50 results
signals.summary: `vercel logs --limit N` with N > 50 returns the same first 50 log entries repeated. The API appears to ignore page offset and always returns the first page while reporting hasMore: true. CLI accumulates duplicates until limit is reached. Makes log retrieval for anything beyond 50 entries entirely broken.
signals.review_reason: Observability tool completely broken for log windows with >50 entries. Every subsequent page returns the same first 50 records while claiming hasMore: true. Direct user impact: developers cannot retrieve full log history. Evidence is explicit and reproducible with provided bash commands. API-level bug (page parameter ignored), affects all users of the CLI.

source_issues.title: vercel logs returns duplicate entries when there are more than 50 results and --limit > 50
source_issues.evidence: Author provides exact bash reproduction commands showing byte-identical duplicates. --since 10min --limit 100 returns 100 total entries but only 50 unique. Root cause identified: API endpoint /api/logs/?page=N ignores the page parameter and always returns first page while reporting pagination.hasMore: true. Broken in CLI 53.1.0 and 53.3.2.

signals.topic: Services-mode with Next.js middleware breaks deployment at 'Deploying outputs' stage with generic error
signals.summary: When a project uses `experimentalServices` (services-mode) with at least one non-root service and the Next.js service has a `middleware.ts`, every deployment fails at 'Deploying outputs...' with a generic error message and no actionable detail. The bug is deterministic: removing middleware.ts allows clean deploys, re-adding it fails. Root cause is middleware routes not being exempted from ownership scoping, corrupting the route's src regex.
aliases: middleware breaks deploys in services mode
signals.review_reason: Main deployment flow is blocked for users of experimentalServices with Next.js middleware. Every deploy fails with generic 'unexpected error' at 'Deploying outputs' stage, no stderr, no actionable detail. Deterministic reproduction with a 5-file sandbox. Users are forced to abandon services-mode entirely as the only workaround. Linked internal support cases confirm real-world customer impact.

source_issues.title: Services-Mode: Middleware routes are not exempted from scopeRoutesToServiceOwnership, breaking deploy outputs
source_issues.evidence: Fully reproducible from a 5-file sandbox. Author provides detailed isolation matrix proving middleware.ts presence is necessary and sufficient trigger. Linked Vercel support cases: 01kpgVUAoxBA9kuW and 01161162. Related community threads confirm broader 'Deploying outputs' failures since 2026-05-07. Workaround: drop services-mode entirely. Generic error with no stderr, exit code, or per-function detail makes this a main-flow blocker.

signals.topic: vercel dev missing Host/Origin header validation allowing unintended request routing
signals.summary: vercel dev accepts HTTP and WebSocket requests without validating the Host or Origin headers against the actual local listen address. This allows requests to be routed based on spoofed headers. Author has disabled vercel dev + web access concurrently until the issue is addressed.
signals.review_reason: Security gap in local dev server allowing Host/Origin header spoofing. While no active exploitation is shown, the author has explicitly disabled functionality as a result. This is a genuine security concern in a development tool that handles HTTP routing. Kept at P2 because: single report, no confirmed active exploitation, and impact is primarily on local dev environments rather than production.

source_issues.title: vercel dev missing Host/Origin validation
source_issues.evidence: Reporter explicitly states they have disabled vercel dev + web access simultaneously until this is addressed. References source code in packages/cli/src/util/dev/server.ts. No active exploitation reported but the lack of header validation creates a class of request-routing vulnerabilities in local dev environments.

signals.topic: Serverless function runtime fails with @rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu module not found
signals.summary: Serverless functions on Vercel crash at runtime with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for @rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu. This is caused by npm's optional dependency bug on Linux. Serverless functions terminate with FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED. Adding the module as an explicit dependency does not resolve the issue, as serverless functions have their own bundling rules.
aliases: rollup native module not found serverless
npm optional dependency missing in vercel functions
signals.review_reason: Serverless functions fail in production for users whose dependencies use @rollup. The underlying cause is an npm bug, but the failure manifests exclusively in Vercel's serverless runtime environment. Workarounds (explicit deps, direct imports) don't work. Kept at P2 because: known root cause external to Vercel (npm bug), but user impact is real — functions fail on production with no Vercel-provided fix path.

source_issues.title: ERROR: @rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu not found for serverless function running on Vercel
source_issues.evidence: Serverless function deployed to Vercel crashes on runtime with exit status 1. Author tried explicit dependency addition and direct imports — neither resolved it. Function INVOCATION_FAILED for end users in production. The underlying cause is npm bug with optional dependencies, but Vercel's serverless environment is where the failure manifests. Issue has been open since 2024-05-28 with 10 comments, indicating ongoing relevance.

signals.topic: MCP HTTP transport fails to handle SSE stream interruptions and timeout resets, causing in-flight requests to hang or be cancelled
signals.summary: Two related transport failures: (a) HTTP SSE stream disconnects cause requests to hang forever with no resumption; (b) Long-running MCP tool calls are cancelled at fixed wall-clock timeout even when server actively streams progress notifications. Both leave agents stuck indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: Two issues with distinct but related root causes in the MCP HTTP transport code. Both cause agent tool calls to hang or fail silently — a critical blocker for AI-assisted workflows. count=2 meets the threshold. The authors provide detailed code-level root cause analysis and log evidence.

source_issues.title: MCP HTTP transport: SSE stream death silently hangs in-flight requests (no resumption)
source_issues.evidence: HTTP/2 RST_STREAM, network disconnects, idle keepalive, or laptop sleep cause SSE reader task to die. Request hangs on spinner forever. Log shows 'http/2 stream closed with error code CANCEL (0x8)'. No Last-Event-ID resumption implemented.

source_issues.title: MCP context server requests cancelled mid-flight despite progress notifications
source_issues.evidence: Long-running MCP tool calls (e.g. cargo test, multi-file code review) are cancelled exactly at context_server_timeout even when server is actively streaming notifications/progress. Wall-clock timer does not reset on inbound frames. Logs show 'http/2 stream closed with error code CANCEL (0x8)'.

signals.topic: Editor completely freezes on startup with no input response (spinning wheel then total unresponsiveness)
signals.summary: After startup, Zed shows a spinning wheel for 2-3 minutes then becomes completely unresponsive — no GUI actions, no shortcuts, only close works.
signals.review_reason: Single-issue P0 due to extreme severity: editor is completely unusable for 2-3+ minutes then permanently unresponsive, leaving users with no recourse except force-close. This is a main-flow block with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Zed doesn't react on any input
source_issues.evidence: User reports Zed shows spinning wheel for 2-3 min after startup on Fedora 44, then becomes completely unresponsive — no GUI actions, no keyboard shortcuts work, only close button functions. Only 1 report but extremely severe as editor is entirely unusable.

signals.topic: Zed crashes with multi_buffer panic when opening large projects
signals.summary: Opening large projects on Windows causes a panic in multi_buffer.rs (offset > snapshot.len()) leading to repeated crashes and data loss.
signals.review_reason: Single-issue P0 because it causes a verified panic with stack trace in multi_buffer.rs on the primary workflow (opening projects). The crash is reproducible, leaves the editor unusable, and involves a data-integrity violation (offset mismatch in text buffer).

source_issues.title: Zed freezes then crashes when opening a large project
source_issues.evidence: Crash trace shows panic in multi_buffer.rs:5183 — 'offset 4621 is greater than snapshot.len() 4562' — triggered when opening a large project with git worktrees on Windows 11. Crash reproduces across multiple restart attempts. Corrupts editing session.

signals.topic: Claude Code (ACP) silently fails to send messages after rapid quit-and-relaunch cycle
signals.summary: After a quick Cmd+Q + reopen cycle, ACP shows 'no branch' and message sending hangs on spinner forever — backend never receives any request. Reproducible by repeatedly quitting and relaunching.
aliases: Codex agent silent failure on relaunch
signals.review_reason: Single-issue P1 with explicit reproducible steps, backend evidence confirming zero outbound requests, and clean logs hiding the failure. Makes ACP entirely unusable for affected users with no error signal to debug. Reliable repro steps provided.

source_issues.title: Codex agent silently fails to respond after rapid quit-and-relaunch cycle
source_issues.evidence: User provides two reliable repro steps: (1) ACP asks for auth -> click 'End current conversation' -> immediately Cmd+Q; or (2) rapid repeated quit-and-relaunch. ACP shows 'no branch' on startup and message spinner hangs forever. Backend logs confirm no request arrives. Log shows clean INFO-level logs with no errors, making this a silent failure.

signals.topic: Terminal panel content overflows beyond visible area, hiding bottom output and command prompt
signals.summary: Terminal panel in a specific project fails to scroll, causing output to overflow beyond the visible area — bottom content and command prompt are unreadable and inaccessible.
aliases: Terminal scroll broken in specific project
signals.review_reason: Single-issue P1 because terminal overflow directly prevents users from reading command output and interacting with the prompt — a core terminal function is completely broken in the affected project. The issue includes a screen recording as evidence.

source_issues.title: Terminal panel content overflows
source_issues.evidence: Terminal content overflows in one specific project/directory, leaving bottom unreadable and command prompt not visible. Zoom-in partially缓解es but does not fully resolve. Affects a specific project while other workspaces work fine, suggesting a project-specific trigger. Terminal is unusable for long-output commands in affected project.
